audit_logging: authorization denials are logged with subject, operation and resource type (no credentials)
authentication: oidc: bearer tokens of issuer https://login.example.com/ for audience 'team-notes-api', algorithms RS256 only (HS*/none refused), signature verified against the JWKS at https://login.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json (TLS verified, private CA only added through oidc_ca_bundle, response capped, cached 300 s, one fetch attempt per 30 s, stale keys served for at most oidc_jwks_stale_max_s), exp/nbf/iat required with 30 s leeway; provider unreachable, failing or unusable is 503, not 401; the client is verified against a local HTTPS provider in tests/test_jwks.py
execution: generated tests run only through the v1.9 trust model, in a copy of the project; the local executor is process hygiene, not a sandbox

multi_tenant.principal_tenant_binding: enforced: the tenant path parameter must equal the verified workspace_id claim of the token, otherwise 403; a token without a valid tenant claim is 401
storage_isolation: tenant_id column on every entity and a tenant filter on every repository query

not_claimed: network or filesystem isolation of executed tests
protection against code the generated tests execute (the trust model is process hygiene, not a sandbox)
business rules beyond the declared policy (roles per operation and ownership are enforced; anything finer is the author's code)
validation against a real identity provider (the JWKS client is verified against a local HTTPS provider with a private CA; a provider's own behaviour is not)
OAuth2 authorization flows (code, PKCE, device), consent, token issuance, refresh tokens or an authorization server (only externally issued tokens are validated)
public resources inside an authenticated API
authorization proven by the name of a dependency (the auditor counts a policy only where its code shows the decision)
resource_authorization: roles_and_ownership: per-operation roles checked in a route dependency before the service runs (403): create needs admin/editor, update needs admin/editor, delete needs admin/editor; ownership of notes.Note: owner_id is the creating principal's subject; reads are tenant-wide, update/delete need the owner or an admin role (admin); enforced in the service and the repository, the router only carries the principal
